requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Verdict: the implementation and tests meet `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.** One marking gap is noted below as minor.

## Implementation

**Initial mandatory set** (`AssessmentSources::prepare`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs`):
- It builds the selectors: the subject, each `{cite}`d declaration, the `{impl}`/`{test}` sources and the anchors.
- It then calls `definition_inputs(..., &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`.
- That function calls `terms::dependencies`, which gathers direct term references from the subject text and from every contributed input.
  - Rust sources are scanned only in comments.
  - Markdown sources are scanned with code protection, so literal roles are skipped.
  - Requirements inputs are scanned through their declaration bodies.
- `close_dependencies` in `src/terms.rs` expands to a fixed point.
  - It uses a `visited` set, so there are no duplicates and cycles terminate.
  - It scans the definition body for further term references.
- Each name becomes an `InputSelector::Definition` resolved by `source_input`.
  - `InputSelector::resolve` returns `target.raw_lines`, the full fenced declaration including the `:phrase:` option.
- `prepare` appends these inputs only if they are not already present.

**Additional reads:**
- `tools::read` and `tools::search` (both marked `{impl}`) call `additional_definitions`.
  - It computes the same transitive set over the newly delivered inputs.
  - It filters out definitions already in those inputs or already recorded.
- The definitions are returned in the tool result, so they are supplied to the model, and they are added to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
- `converse` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) puts delivered inputs in `pending` and calls `record_inputs` after the next successful response.
  - That happens before any submission is parsed, so the definitions are recorded before a submission is accepted.
- `record_inputs` deduplicates recorded inputs.

All of these code sites carry `{impl}` markers.

**Marking gap (minor):**
- `prepare_citation` also calls `definition_inputs` but has no `{impl}` for this requirement.
- The deciding logic is in the marked helpers, and `prepare_citation` only calls them, so I do not count it as a gap.
- Two parallel tool calls in one turn could each deliver the same new definition, because `pending` is not consulted. The evidence record is still deduplicated, so this does not violate the requirement.

## Tests

- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (`inputs.rs`) covers the initial set.
  - `terms.unit` and `terms.value` reference each other, so this is a cycle.
  - It asserts exactly two definition inputs, so the transitive closure has no duplicates and the cycle terminates.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` covers the failure case of an unstaged term file. The error is reported, and the term is included once staged.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (`mod.rs`) covers additional reads.
  - A read of `fn[work]` introduces `terms.value`, and its transitive dependency `terms.unit` is introduced through a cycle.
  - It asserts that the evidence contains `[terms.unit, terms.value]` exactly once each, with full `:::{definition}` and `:phrase:` text.
  - It asserts that the definition text is absent from the first request and present in the second, so it was delivered before submission.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` covers the `habeas` tool. It checks the definitions in the result, recording, and deduplication on repeated recording.
- `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` covers `ripgrep`: terminology is supplied and recorded.
- `src/terms.rs` has a dependency test, which covers literal-role skipping and missing-term errors.

Boundaries covered: cycles, transitivity, dedup, missing and unstaged terms, and the ordering of delivery before submission. No acknowledged FIXMEs.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
